motivation: The existing encoder prompt explicitly requests only a binary review decision and groups uncertainty with affirmation. Test whether explicitly asking for assertion status recovers a distinction that the binary-conditioned representation suppresses.
population: Original development only: deterministically choose 32 cases per language and assertion class by SHA256 of token-input identity. Total 256 developer-exposed cases, balanced over four assertion classes. No regression, calibration or final test is used.
model: Pinned original Gemma4 base with all v9 task-adapter output matrices zeroed. Use its original vocabulary head, not a fitted classifier. No parameter updates.
prediction: Compare original vocabulary logits for four single-token answer letters A/B/C/D. Record conditional probabilities, total probability mass on those letters and unconstrained argmax agreement. These conditional probabilities are not calibrated uncertainty.
purpose: A development diagnostic to decide whether semantic-query representations justify a new training architecture. This sample cannot qualify a release or establish independent superiority.
